thesis: James Hardie fell about 3.0% to $29.05 on 10.7x volume (about 102M shares). S&P Dow Jones Indices announced on Nov 6 that it joins the S&P MidCap 400, replacing Roku, before the open on Nov 11, so today's volume is the index-funds' close-of-day rebalancing trade; one analyst estimated about 79M shares of passive demand. That is a mechanical move, not new company information. The litigation check found an Australian shareholder class action over 2025 disclosures (served June 2026), which the company says it will defend, plus earlier class actions and plaintiff-firm sign-ups, with no hearing date found and no restatement. A mechanical, index-driven move makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: Company-specific results, not index flows, drive a re-rating.
sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices (index change, Nov 6): https://press.spglobal.com/2026-11-06-James-Hardie-Industries-Set-to-Join-S-P-MidCap-400

thesis: Dropbox slipped about 0.6% to $32.40 on 7.3x volume, and this run found no company disclosure or analyst action explaining the volume; coverage notes only an earlier 9% workforce cut and a technology-chief departure, undated in the results. Litigation checks found a pending reconsideration decision in the Entangled Media patent case (hearing Nov 2; the company calls it not material) and a Delaware challenge to the Nevada reincorporation in motion-to-dismiss briefing, with no scheduled ruling and no restatement. Heavy volume with no identified company catalyst leaves the read unresolved, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: A company-specific catalyst emerges and revenue growth re-accelerates.

thesis: First Advantage fell about 8.4% to $21.55 on 7.1x volume after Silver Lake priced an underwritten secondary offering of 15M shares at $21.80 (the company receives no proceeds), following a 12.5M-share sale in August; Silver Lake held about 43% beforehand, and up to 5.3M more shares may be distributed to its limited partners outside the lock-up. The underlying Nov 5 Q3 report (8-K) was a beat and raise: revenue grew 13.8% to $465.8M, adjusted EBITDA was $136.5M (29.3% margin), and full-year revenue guidance was raised to $1.72-1.745B from $1.67-1.71B. The share offering meets the dilution_risk criterion as written, and continued sponsor selling is an open supply overhang. Litigation checks found only plaintiff-firm data-breach investigations (2024 and 2025 incidents), with no filed case, ruling or restatement found. A risk flag present makes this low.
invalidation: Sponsor selling ends and the raised guidance is delivered.

thesis: Fox eased about 0.4% to $67.44 on 5.3x volume. It closed the Roku acquisition on Nov 6, issuing 0.9799 Class A shares plus $95.30 in cash per Roku share, and on Nov 10 began an approximately $8B bond sale to repay the $8.4B bridge loan that funded the cash portion. Today's volume coincides with that financing and with deal-close index flows. The share issuance to Roku holders meets the dilution_risk criterion. Smartmatic's $2.7B defamation case remains in pretrial proceedings with no trial date set. A dilutive, debt-funded deal with a mechanical volume spike makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: Integration synergies and Roku platform growth lift earnings per share despite the larger share count and debt.

thesis: LifeStance slipped about 0.3% to $14.55 on 5.0x volume as its 45M-share secondary offering by selling stockholders, priced at $13.12, moves toward closing on or about Nov 12; the company receives no proceeds and agreed to repurchase 2M of the shares from the underwriters, leaving about 378.2M shares outstanding. The share offering meets the dilution_risk criterion as written. Litigation checks found a 2026 data-privacy class settlement of a little over $3M (no admission) and older 2021-2023 plaintiff-firm investigations, with no scheduled ruling or restatement. With a risk flag present, this is low.
invalidation: Shares hold above the $13.12 offering price after closing and growth continues without further sponsor selling.

thesis: GFL Environmental fell about 7.6% to $42.40 on 4.4x volume after its board ended a four-month strategic review and rejected a roughly $22B take-private bid from a Blackstone, KKR and Energy Capital Partners group, which declined to raise its $52-a-share offer toward the $58 the board sought. The takeover premium built into the shares during the review is unwinding, and RBC flagged possible further downside. Management said the company has never had a better outlook and targets doubling free cash flow per share over five years, but that is a forward goal, not a confirmed result; Q3 EPS of $0.19 missed the $0.20 consensus despite 27% revenue growth. Litigation checks found only older 2020 short-report-related investigations and open NLRB charges, with no restatement in the last 3 years. A premium unwind with an unresolved re-rating makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: Delivered free-cash-flow growth re-rates the shares on fundamentals.

thesis: Clorox rose about 0.9% to $106.46 on 3.4x volume, and this run found no catalyst dated today. Its Nov 2 fiscal Q1 2027 report showed net sales up 33% and adjusted EPS of $1.55 vs $1.07 consensus, but about 18 points of organic growth came from lapping a prior-year ERP inventory drawdown and about 15 points from the GOJO acquisition. Gross margin fell 130bp, the input-cost inflation estimate rose about $40M to $240M, and management now expects adjusted EPS near the low end of its $5.70-6.00 range. Clorox is the plaintiff in its $380M Cognizant cyberattack suit; no adverse litigation or restatement was found. A headline beat flattered by one-offs and offset by margin pressure leaves the evidence mixed, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Gross margin recovers and EPS tracks toward the middle of the range.

thesis: Csquare rose about 14.7% to $17.52 on 3.2x volume after its Q3 report: revenue grew 25.6% to $302.3M against a $281.5M estimate, adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $490-500M from $460-480M, and TD Cowen raised its target to $30. The loss of $0.58 a share was wider than expected, partly from about $58.6M of IPO-related costs. The July 17 IPO (50M shares at $21) falls outside the ~90-day dilution window. Against that, an Oct 22 Dalrymple Finance short report questioned the company's cash flows and capital structure, the Q2 10-Q showed operating cash flow down about 49%, and several plaintiff firms are investigating, with no filed case and no company rebuttal found in this run. A strong quarter set against unresolved short-report questions leaves the evidence unresolved, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Operating cash flow recovers and the short-report claims are rebutted.
sources: Business Wire (plaintiff-firm investigation after short report): https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261025367841/en/CSQR-Investors-with-$100000-in-Losses-Have-Opportunity-to-Join-Csquare-Inc.-Fraud-Investigation-with-SBS-Law

thesis: TG Therapeutics reported Q3 2026 on Nov 9 (8-K) and raised full-year guidance: total global revenue to about $1B from about $950M, and BRIUMVI U.S. net product revenue to $915-920M from $890-905M. Q3 BRIUMVI U.S. revenue grew about 52% to $232.6M, and it repurchased about $100M of stock in the quarter. The shares rose about 1.3% to $64.20 on 3.2x volume, after touching a 52-week high of $68.03 intraday. Counter-evidence named and not resolved: quarterly revenue of $259.9M fell short of the ~$269.5M estimate, so the raise depends on a stronger Q4. Litigation and governance checks found a July 2026 plaintiff-firm solicitation about possible self-dealing and an older 2022 securities case, with no filed 2026 complaint, scheduled ruling or restatement. A confirmed, company-specific raise with an open revenue-miss counter-case puts this at medium.
invalidation: Q4 BRIUMVI revenue falls short of the raised guide, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$59.83).

thesis: Take-Two rose about 8.3% to $224.66 on 2.9x volume after its fiscal Q2 2027 report: net bookings fell about 18% and revenue about 15% year over year, but management kept full-year net bookings guidance at $8.0-8.2B, guided Q3 net bookings to $3.35-3.5B, and said Grand Theft Auto VI pre-orders are tracking far in excess of its initial expectations ahead of the Nov 19 launch. Counter-evidence named and not resolved: the current quarter was weak, the pre-order commentary is unquantified, and the launch itself is still pending. Litigation checks found GTA VI leak subpoenas, plaintiff-firm solicitations tied to the 2025 delay, and a UK employment tribunal over Rockstar dismissals, with no scheduled ruling found; the SEC stock-option settlement and restatement date to 2007-2009, outside the 3-year window. A company-specific catalyst that is still pending puts this at medium.
invalidation: GTA VI launch sales disappoint or full-year bookings guidance is cut, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$207.40).

thesis: Alcon reported Q3 2026 on Nov 10: sales grew 5% to $2.7B and core EPS of $0.91 beat the $0.89 estimate, but it tightened full-year sales growth to about 6%, nine-month reported EPS fell about 40% on a $402M charge for discontinuing PowerVision programs, and revenue roughly matched estimates. The shares slipped about 1.2% to $74.25 on 2.7x volume and traded near $70.51 after hours, and this run found no coverage explaining the reaction. Litigation checks found 2026 consumer class actions over recalled Systane and GenTeal eye drops (sterility labeling) and a preservative-free labeling suit, with no scheduled ruling and no restatement. A modest beat against a tightened outlook and a weak post-market tape leaves the evidence mixed, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Growth re-accelerates on product launches and the recall-related issues fade.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV rose about 1.2% to $41.17, and this run's search found no new company disclosure dated today. It remains well above the ~$34.92 pre-announcement level. The thesis rests on the company's Nov 9 fiscal Q2 release cited in the prior thesis: LISRAYA (brepocitinib) generated $31.0M of net product revenue in its first five weeks after August approval, and cash and securities were $4.2B. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the non-infectious uveitis sNDA is not expected until 1H calendar 2027, so that indication is not yet approved. An Investor Day is set for Dec 9. This stays medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls, or FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene rose about 2.4% to $70.21, above the ~$68.03 pre-report level, and this run found no company disclosure dated today. The thesis rests on the company-specific Oct 27 Q3 report: EPS of $0.58, a consolidated HBR of 92.7% better than expected, and 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $5.20. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: roughly $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 EPS, Medicaid membership declines and margin pressure, the 2027 Arkansas Medicaid expansion exit, and the Lunstrum v. Centene class action with no scheduled ruling. These cap this at medium.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal; trimmed toward its low-conviction target on Nov 9). NWL rose about 0.8% to $5.94, slightly above the $5.82 cost, and this run's search found no new company disclosure. It remains above the ~$5.08 pre-report invalidation level. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and keep the evidence mixed: the Oct 30 Q3 report cut the operating cash flow outlook about 62% to $150M, cited about $220M of inflation headwinds and a $101M impairment, and only maintained full-year adjusted EPS guidance. The early-exit guard applies (the opening buy was 5 trading days ago), and there is no new fact, so the direction stays long. This stays low, and the stop-loss and conviction-trim still protect the position.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or the cash-flow outlook is cut again, a further impairment, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).
sources: Newell Brands IR (latest items, none dated Nov 10): https://ir.newellbrands.com/news-releases/news-release-details/newell-brands-announces-agreement-carl-c-icahn/

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 9 on the Nov 6 proposal). JFrog eased about 4.3% to $103.51 after Monday's 52-week high, and this run's search found no new company disclosure dated today. The thesis rests on the Nov 5 Q3 report (8-K): revenue grew 31% to $179.2M, cloud revenue grew 60%, net dollar retention rose to 124%, and free cash flow was $66.5M. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: GAAP operating income is still slightly negative, share-based compensation was $41.8M in the quarter, the Q4 revenue guide implies only about 2-3% sequential growth, and the size of any full-year raise against prior guidance remains unconfirmed. The early-exit guard applies (opened 1 trading day ago). This stays medium.
invalidation: Cloud growth or net dollar retention decelerates materially, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$74.62).
